fatal_errors: The proposed intervention is MoS2 addition to AlCoCrFeNiTi, whereas the target intervention is varying matrix Mo content in CoCrFeNiMox composites already containing Ni-coated MoS2, Ag, and Cr2O3.
The claim that an MoS2-based film remains effective to approximately 800 °C is not supported by the cited evidence, which explicitly describes good MoS2 lubrication below 400 °C.

The proposed suppression of oxidation contradicts the target high-temperature mechanism, in which oxidation and tribochemical formation of NiO and silver-molybdate glazes are essential to lubrication at 600–800 °C.
The predicted consistent 30–50% friction reduction and order-of-magnitude wear reduction through 800 °C are unsupported by the cited excerpts.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the general objective and proposes a controlled temperature-dependent tribology experiment, so it has reasonable problem alignment and falsifiability. However, it reconstructs a different material system, intervention, and baseline. It captures only the low-temperature lamellar-lubrication role of MoS2 and omits Mo-induced lattice distortion, sigma-phase strengthening, Ag-assisted lubrication, and high-temperature oxide/silver-molybdate glaze formation. Its central wide-temperature mechanism is especially weak because the cited evidence limits established MoS2 performance to below 400 °C rather than supporting persistence to 800 °C. The experiment could test the alternative claim, but SEM/EDS alone would not adequately establish a specific MoS2 tribofilm or distinguish it from oxides and molybdates; Raman or XPS would be needed.
